kind: HISTORICAL BACKTEST (hypothetical, not forward paper results)
weight_rule: fundamental factor (20%) removed; remaining five weights renormalised proportionally (divide by 0.80), identical to the live engine when fundamentals are unavailable for a symbol
caveats: SURVIVORSHIP BIAS: universe = CURRENT S&P 500 + Nasdaq-100 members (no historical constituents on the free stack). Failed/delisted names are absent, so stock-strategy results are biased UPWARD; buy&hold SPY/QQQ are unaffected.

NO POINT-IN-TIME FUNDAMENTALS: yfinance exposes only current fundamentals, so the swing backtest drops the fundamental factor (20% weight) and renormalises the other five. The live swing strategy uses fundamentals when available.
Prices are Yahoo split-adjusted daily bars; dividends are ignored (understates buy&hold slightly). Data errors are possible.
Spread/slippage are modelled (liquidity-tiered half-spread + 5 bps slippage), not observed quotes. No market impact, halts or partial fills.
Parameters are fixed a priori and were NOT tuned on these data; the 'out-of-sample' split is a pre-declared date, not a fitted one. Windows are anchored walk-forward evaluations without refitting.
Small RM10,000 account with whole shares: expensive stocks are unaffordable, which shapes results (and is the real constraint).

PARITY: this run uses the live engine's gating/sizing/exit code except fundamentals (not point-in-time available) and delayed 5-minute fills (daily bars: next-session open). See docs/BACKTEST_LIVE_PARITY.md.
Forward-accumulating point-in-time fundamentals snapshots started 2026-10-12 (table fundamentals_pit); they cannot be used for past dates.

legacy.label: LEGACY (not validated for the current live strategy)
headline: Out-of-sample (2024-): swing 40.9% / mean-reversion -2.5% vs buy&hold SPY 59.9% / QQQ 79.0% (USD, after modelled costs).
Swing had lower drawdown (OOS max DD -7.9% vs SPY -17.9%) but did NOT beat passive SPY/QQQ on return in either period.
Mean-reversion lost money after costs (OOS -2.5%, in-sample -6.5%) with high turnover: not recommended as configured.
No strategy is declared a winner; buy&hold remains the benchmark to beat. All numbers are hypothetical backtests with survivorship bias; they are NOT forward results.
